function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

The command would be something like:

echo Reminder: Subscribe to Netflix > C:\Users\<username>\Documents\Netflix_Subscription_Reminder_2026-03-27.txt

But we don't know the username. We can use environment variable %USERPROFILE% to refer to the user's profile directory. So:

echo Reminder: Subscribe to Netflix > %USERPROFILE%\Documents\Netflix_Subscription_Reminder_2026-03-27.txt

We can also add date stamp inside the file. But the user just wants a note. So we can do that.

We need to call the function with command: "echo Reminder: Subscribe to Netflix > %USERPROFILE%\\Documents\\Netflix_Subscription_Reminder_2026-03-27.txt"
